population.label: World population (UN projection)
population.hint: How many people the world will feed depends on choices families make, shaped by education, health care and access to voluntary family planning. These are the UN's projections, not a lever. The levers' effect is measured against the future you pick.

chart.caption: The shaded area behind the lines is the world population, on the right axis. It shows estimates for the past, then the UN projection or the number of people on Earth set in the panel. With a UN projection and Population growth as farming's future, farm emissions grow with the population. The rest of the world's emissions follow their own scenario. A number of people set in the panel changes every human emission.

people.label: People on Earth in {year}
people.hint: How many people live on Earth by the year every lever is in place. Every human emission changes with that number: farming, energy, industry, transport, buildings, land clearing and air pollution. At 0, human emissions stop. The cleaner air warms the planet for a few years. After that, the carbon dioxide already in the air keeps it warm.
